subject: Checkout latency/429 tailstorm — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Alex Miller <alex.miller@nimbus.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05 09:12 -0700
Subject: Anomalous p99 latency + 429s impacting checkout

Hi Dylan / Redwood team,

We started seeing a correlated spike in p95/p99 latency and a sharp increase in 429 responses hitting our checkout API at ~09:05 PDT. This affected ~12% of checkout attempts over a ~20 minute window and caused payment retries on our side. Sample request IDs and timestamps are attached (request-samples.txt).

Observations from our side:
- p50 unchanged, p95 went from ~280ms to ~1.2s, p99 to ~3.9s.
- 429s increased from baseline ~0.1% to ~8% during the window.
- Our clients implement exponential backoff but several retries piled up and we saw amplification on our side as well.

Can you confirm whether there was a change on Redwood's hosted API (rate limiter, model swap, or rollout) that could have triggered a retry amplification? This is impacting a live promo — we need a mitigation and a timeline for RCA.

Attaching logs and a short clip of traces (nimbus-checkout-logs-20261005.zip).

Thanks,
Alex
SRE Lead, Nimbus Commerce
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@nimbus.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05 09:24 -0700
Subject: Re: Anomalous p99 latency + 429s impacting checkout

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're treating this as high priority.

Immediate steps:
1) I've looped in SRE (Jonas) and Product (Marissa) to investigate correlates on our side.
2) Can you confirm whether all requests were routed to the hosted API (not Dedicated) and share any client retry settings you have?
3) We'll run an emergency mitigation (rate limiter softening + circuit-breaker) if we see retry amplification originating from our side.

We'll post live updates to this thread. ETA for first actionable update: 30 minutes.

— Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05 09:27 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Nimbus p99 spike — possible retry storm (investigate + mitigate)

Team — Alex sent logs showing a sudden p99 jump and a ~8% 429 rate clustered at 09:05 PDT. Key asks:
- Check our rate limiter logs for sudden throttle policy changes or global token bucket exhaustion.
- Correlate deploy history (any canary/fallbacks) and model variant rollouts around 09:00–09:10.
- Look at ingress spikes (burst concurrency) and downstream model latency variance.

Immediate mitigations to consider (please execute if safe):
- Activate stricter per-client soft circuit-breaker to return 503 early to avoid pile-up, or temporarily increase per-client burst window to let inflight requests through.
- Enable reject-fast policy for known retry patterns to avoid queue saturation.
- Temporarily route Nimbus traffic to a lower-latency model variant with smaller context window to reduce token latency.

I can call into the SRE bridge if helpful.

— Dylan
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05 09:38 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Nimbus p99 spike — possible retry storm (investigate + mitigate)

Taking this. Quick findings:
- No config rollouts at 09:00. No model swaps in the Canary pipeline.
- We observed a multi-region influx from a small set of originating IPs tied to Nimbus (see ingress logs). Requests spiked concurrency and our global token bucket hit a short exhaustion event at 09:06:12. That caused a high transient 429 rate.
- Many clients retried aggressively (our traces show repeated same-request IDs), which amplified tail latency as the system attempted to requeue in-flight tokens.

Actions executed (09:38):
- Deployed circuit-breaker rule: immediate 503 on >8 retries per minute per client and tightened token-bucket refill for the affected pool. Commit: commit:2a7c9b (infra/rate-limiter).
- Enabled a targeted routing change to route Nimbus to the low-latency variant (model-lite-v2) for 1 hour.
- Opened JIRA INFRA-1423 and linked to incident docs.

We'll monitor for stabilization. Attaching a short SRE timeline (sre-timeline.txt).

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@nimbus.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency/429 tailstorm — urgent escalation

Alex — quick update and apologizes for the disruption. Jonas pushed mitigations (circuit-breaker + routing to model-lite-v2). We are seeing early signs of recovery in your metrics (p99 trending down from ~3.9s to ~780ms).

Next steps:
- SRE will continue to monitor for 60 minutes; conditioned on stability we'll keep Nimbus on the lite variant for 4 hours to avoid regressions during your promo window.
- Product will prepare a root cause summary; we'll share a postmortem and a proposed client-side backoff pattern that reduces retry amplification risk.
- I have looped in Vivek to make an exec-level offer (service credit + prioritized RCA).

Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Miller <alex.miller@nimbus.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05 12:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency/429 tailstorm — urgent escalation

Thanks — I can confirm a strong reduction in 429s and p99 from our dashboard. We'll keep monitoring for the next hour.

Couple of asks before we close the incident:
1) Formal RCA with timeline and the exact root cause (was it ingress burst from our client-side behavior, or did something on the rate-limiter side exacerbate things?).
2) A recommended client backoff pattern (we can adopt a jittered exponential backoff + capped retries).
3) Requesting a billing credit for the outage window — I'll let our procurement team open a formal request, but please flag.

Appreciate the quick triage; please keep me posted to this thread.

— Alex
SRE Lead, Nimbus Commerce
